posts.title: Financing primary care after the donors leave
posts.excerpt: The post-donor transition is treated as a budgeting exercise. It is really a question about who holds the risk when the external money stops.
posts.body:
The post-donor transition is treated as a budgeting exercise. It is really a question about who holds the risk when the external money stops — and most systems have never asked it out loud.

This is sample content. Log in at /admin to replace it with the full essay.

posts.title: The quiet cost of heroic managers
posts.excerpt: Every team has the person who absorbs the chaos. The trouble is that their heroism is also why the chaos never gets fixed.

posts.title: Models don't have judgment. Systems do.
posts.excerpt: The interesting question was never whether the model is accurate. It's what the clinic does with a number it half-trusts at 2am.

posts.title: The continuum of care is a promise, not a diagram
posts.excerpt: We draw it as a clean line from pregnancy to old age. Patients experience it as a series of cliffs.

posts.title: Reform as a coalition problem
posts.excerpt: Good policy fails when it's treated as a design problem instead of what it actually is: a question of who you can keep on side.

posts.title: Why reorganisations fail before they begin
posts.excerpt: By the time the new org chart is announced, the real decisions have already happened in the corridor.

posts.title: What a clinic actually wants from an algorithm
posts.excerpt: Not accuracy. Not explainability. It wants to not be blamed when it follows the recommendation and the patient still dies.

posts.title: Who pays for the health system we say we want
posts.excerpt: Universal coverage is a budget line that nobody wants to own. Until that changes, the rest is rhetoric.
